title_en: Yang Dewang — crime of insulting a corpse
keywords_en: Criminal; Crime of insulting a corpse; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Hubei Province; Natural person; Criminal Law; Whether skeletal remains constitute a corpse; Elements of the crime of insulting a corpse; Affirm the original judgment; Exhuming a grave and destroying a corpse; Superstitious exorcism; Relocation of a grave
full_text_en:
Yang Dewang — crime of insulting a corpse

Prosecutor: People's Procuratorate of Changyang Tujia Autonomous County, Hubei Province.

Defendant: Yang Dewang, male, 51 years old, of Tujia ethnicity, a farmer from Changyang Tujia Autonomous County, Hubei Province. Arrested on March 9, 1998.

Defense Counsel: Xu Guisong, lawyer from Hengping Law Firm, Changyang Tujia Autonomous County, Hubei Province.

The People's Procuratorate of Changyang Tujia Autonomous County, Hubei Province, instituted a public prosecution against the defendant Yang Dewang on the charge of insulting a corpse, and filed the case with the Changyang Tujia Autonomous County People's Court.

The indictment by the People's Procuratorate of Changyang Tujia Autonomous County alleged: The defendant Yang Dewang insulted the corpse of another person, and his act has violated Article 302 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting the crime of insulting a corpse. It requested a judgment according to law.

The defendant Yang Dewang did not raise any objection to the charges by the prosecutorial authority. The defense counsel Xu Guisong also did not raise any objection to the charges, but argued that the defendant Yang Dewang's criminal circumstances were minor, the social harm was small, and he had a good attitude of admitting guilt after being brought to justice, and suggested that the collegial panel impose a lighter punishment or grant an exemption from punishment.

The Changyang Tujia Autonomous County People's Court found through trial that: The deceased Liu had a close relationship with the defendant Yang Dewang and often accompanied Yang on his work trips. Later, a conflict arose between them, and they ceased contact, harboring grudges. On September 11, 1997, Liu committed suicide by taking poison after his extramarital affair was exposed. After Liu's death, Yang Dewang suffered from rheumatism causing pain throughout his body. He suspected that because he had told others about Liu's improper sexual relationship, Liu's spirit was now haunting him for revenge, causing his illness. He thus conceived the idea of relocating Liu's grave and destroying the corpse. From February 15 to 27, 1998, Yang Dewang went to Liu's grave three times. He dug open the grave, pried open the coffin, used a sickle to strike Liu's head which was still covered by a towel, removed Liu's skull, and moved the skull and five coffin boards to be buried in his own contracted responsibility farmland. He also used a hoe to scatter the remaining parts of Liu's corpse and other burial items and discarded them in the original grave pit, all in order to drive away Liu's "spirit." After the incident, Liu's relatives and local residents expressed deep indignation at Yang Dewang's conduct.

The above facts are confirmed by the report statement of Liu Zongyan, a relative of the deceased; testimonies of witnesses such as Ruan Zhiyuan, Yu Jifu, Li Zuomei, Li Zhihua, and Liu Zaixiang; and evidence including photographs of the corpse remains at the scene and photographs of the grave. The defendant Yang Dewang also confessed. The facts are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient.

The Changyang Tujia Autonomous County People's Court held that: The defendant Yang Dewang, driven by ignorant thoughts, secretly excavated another person's grave and insulted the corpse, harming social customs and disrupting public order. His act has violated Article 302 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and constitutes the crime of insulting a corpse. The charges by the prosecutorial authority are established, and the court confirms them. After being brought to justice, Yang Dewang had a relatively good attitude of admitting guilt, and thus a lighter punishment may be imposed at the court's discretion. In order to maintain social order and social customs and to uphold the law, the Changyang Tujia Autonomous County People's Court rendered the judgment on April 17, 1998:

The defendant Yang Dewang is convicted of the crime of insulting a corpse and sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Yang Dewang refused to accept it and appealed on the grounds that he was merely driven by superstitious thoughts and fear of being haunted by ghosts, so he relocated Liu's grave; he did not intend to insult Liu's corpse; moreover, Liu in the grave had already turned into white bones and was not a corpse; therefore his conduct did not meet the constitutive elements of the crime of insulting a corpse.

The Yichang Intermediate People's Court, Hubei Province, held upon trial that the facts found by the original trial were clear, and the evidence was reliable and sufficient. Although partial remains of Liu's corpse had become skeletonized more than five months after death, the grave had not been moved, and the entire corpse had not disintegrated, so it should be regarded as a complete corpse. The appellant Yang Dewang, driven by superstitious thoughts, excavated the grave and destroyed the corpse. Objectively, his conduct bore the characteristics of insulting a corpse. In fact, his acts of grave excavation and corpse destruction hurt the feelings of Liu's relatives, harmed social customs, and disrupted public order, thus constituting the crime of insulting a corpse. His grounds of appeal were untenable. The original trial's conviction and sentencing of Yang Dewang were appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. The Yichang Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on July 30, 1998, ruled:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.
